solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spread out here in child’s play zone

blocks.note: a picnic is something very easy, just like child's play
a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: A spot in a playground where children's games sprawl across the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: this is a place where you spread out a rug and food. 'No picnic' means hard, so a picnic is something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors lay out blankets and meals at such a designated outdoor spot, so it is literally a place where things are spread.

clue.text: Old Republicans about to jump up and down

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the joined letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
the Grand Old Party is the nickname of the US Republican Party

explanation.surface: Elderly members of a political party are about to start bouncing with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: To pogo is to dance by leaping straight up and down on the spot, as punks did, after the spring-loaded stick toy.

blocks.note: surface reading: a lesson taught in a primary school
setter's reading: a school subject that is all about the chemical elements

explanation.walkthrough: 'Elementary school' suggests young children, but here elementary means concerned with elements.
explanation.definitionFit: This science studies elements and compounds and how they react, so it is the school subject devoted to elementary matter.

clue.text: I spin around and sound provocative?

indicators.note: around suggests letters spun and scattered about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
sound reasoning is rational, logical

explanation.surface: A spin doctor admits that turning a story makes it sound provocative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a verb meaning seem, but it is the adjective meaning sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that provokes thought or stirs people to act can be called inspiring, so the two words are loose synonyms, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Real gold, so it turns cold

indicators.note: something that turns faces the other way, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
so and then both mean therefore
taken as written, then turned round
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Genuine gold, it turns out, feels cold to the touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine, real and authentic are standard synonyms describing something that is what it claims to be.

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its inner part, so only its core letters are kept

blocks.note: the middle five letters of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A grim scene sits at the heart of a television police drama.
explanation.walkthrough: ELLIS was a British TV detective series starring Sharon D Clarke as DCI Ellis.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a British television crime series featuring a senior detective investigating murders, so it fits a police drama.

blocks.note: first meaning: understand, cotton on
second meaning: a small thin branch

explanation.surface: Someone receives a little criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a bit of stick' reads as being told off; the phrase splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British use the verb means to realise or understand, while the noun is a slender shoot from a tree.

blocks.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
a jam, like a hole, is a tight spot or difficulty

explanation.surface: Breakfast talk: a glass of milk with jam on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-fat milk with none of its cream removed is sold under this adjective, as opposed to skimmed.

blocks.note: great means eminent, famous
Robert Falcon Scott led the doomed expedition to the South Pole

explanation.surface: Someone introduces a famous explorer as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive, but it is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned exclamations of astonishment, so either can stand in for the other as a cry.

indicators.note: out of here means removed from, so some letters are taken away

blocks.note: an inn is a pub, and the apostrophe s is read as a plural
the best-known brand of stout

explanation.surface: A smart bar has run out of dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing INNS from GUINNESS leaves GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy that something is so is to suppose or imagine it, a sense close to conjecture.

clue.text: Elope then set out to find ring

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters are laid out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple run off to marry and then look for a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' wants to be the wedding band in this picture; it is the verb meaning call.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is British for calling them, which means to use the phone; the noun-verb sense of calling fits.

clue.text: He gets second place in this

definitions.text: He gets second place in this

blocks.clueFragment: He gets second place in this
blocks.note: surface reading: some man finishes runner-up in a contest
setter's reading: He is the symbol for helium, element number two

explanation.walkthrough: 'He' reads as a pronoun, but it is helium, which sits second after hydrogen in the chemists' chart.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart of chemical elements is ordered by atomic number, and helium, number two, occupies its second slot.

clue.text: Case of picking up, but not by force

definitions.text: Case of picking up, but not by force

blocks.clueFragment: Case of picking up, but not by force
blocks.note: surface reading: lifting something gently without using strength
setter's reading: a detention made by a member of the public, not by the police force

explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking up' is slang for taking someone into custody, and 'force' means the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an ordinary person may detain someone caught committing a crime, a detention carried out without any police officer.

blocks.note: a spell is a period of time
bound to happen means sure to happen

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person was carried off through time, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests travel; here it means enraptured.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away by delight or wonder, as if held by a magic charm.

indicators.note: moving letters shifts them about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patrol stops as it moves past a remote military post.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something is to end or prevent it, the same as bringing it to a standstill.

clue.text: Bird cooked around noon for China correspondent?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a pen is a female swan
fried is one way of cooking
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A recipe for a bird cooked at midday, sent by a reporter in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang: china plate means mate, so a China correspondent is a friend who writes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal exchanges letters with a mate, often abroad, so a mate who writes is that kind of correspondent.

blocks.note: taken as written
RC is the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: A priest is dismissed from his church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests dismissal; here it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric spark leaping across a gap between electrodes is a luminous electrical discharge of that name.

clue.text: Some dreamer, I can ask for US songs?

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters lie inside the words

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the next three

explanation.surface: A daydreamer wonders whether they may request American tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: The term covers things typical of the US, including a style of roots music drawing on folk and country, hence the question mark.

blocks.note: first meaning: as a hen does with eggs
second meaning: a short poem or ballad meant to be sung

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to put out a single.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen produces eggs by this verb, and the same word is an old literary noun for a ballad or short narrative poem.

clue.text: Unwillingly going home (also happy about it)

indicators.note: also means as well, so a second piece is added after the first
about means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: at home is in
content means satisfied, happy
it refers back to home, so the same two letters again

explanation.surface: Someone is going home reluctantly, yet secretly glad about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket is read literally: besides home, you also need happy placed around 'it', which points back to home, so home is used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking control of the bladder or bowels means relieving oneself involuntarily, a delicate euphemism for going.

clue.text: Quiz show (if you take it you leave it)

definitions.text: if you take it you leave it

blocks.note: first meaning: a long-running BBC Radio 4 general knowledge contest

blocks.clueFragment: if you take it you leave it
blocks.note: second meaning, read cryptically: take the letters I and T out of the country's name and what is left is the first word

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside about a take-it-or-leave-it offer, but it describes the title itself: BRITAIN without IT leaves BRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The programme is a long-running British general knowledge contest crowning one champion each year, so it is a quiz show.

indicators.note: something that retreats goes backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: raw skin is red and sore
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: During battle, a communist army falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Army' looks like the Soviet force, but the words split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Countries engaged in fighting are said to be in a state of conflict, the idiom for being in combat.

clue.text: Botany seminars covering origin of life

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece holds another inside
the origin of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: fora is a plural of forum, a meeting for discussion
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Botany seminars cover the origins of life on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: The plants of a region are its plant life, the subject matter that botany studies, so the definition is loose.

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning see, as in lo and behold
a green light is approval, an okay

explanation.surface: Watch for the traffic signal to turn green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the interjection; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To look happy or tired is to seem or give that impression, so the verb fits appear.

indicators.note: loose letters are not held in place, so they can be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A distasteful hint appears on the TV chat show Loose Women.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose Women is a British daytime TV talk show, but 'Loose' must be split off from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is disagreeable or not wanted, as distasteful things are.

clue.text: I stand before Charlie and I like it

blocks.note: first meaning: the NATO alphabet word for B, which comes just before C
second meaning: a cry of approval from an audience

explanation.surface: Someone stands up in front of a person called Charlie and says they approve.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is the radio code word for C, and this answer is the code word for the letter before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phonetic alphabet the code word for B precedes Charlie, and the same word is shouted to applaud a performance.

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of Douglas Adams's holistic detective, surnamed Gently
second meaning: a long Scottish dagger

explanation.surface: A detective calmly hands over a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gently' looks like an adverb but is the detective's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish Highland short sword or long knife carries this name, a straightforward synonym for a stabbing blade.

blocks.note: to land someone with a burden is to saddle them with it
at the back means behind

explanation.surface: There is some ground lying behind a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like a noun for ground; it is the verb meaning burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge with a dip between two summits, shaped like a saddle, is named for that shape; Blencathra in the Lake District has this alternative name.
